top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at La Ruta de los Conquistadores. Practice on mountain bike stage race — gravel, technical: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 162 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic La Ruta de los Conquistadores' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
162 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
32,300ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At La Ruta de los Conquistadores, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
32,300ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
199ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 162 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at La Ruta de los Conquistadores. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of La Ruta de los Conquistadores. Train it until it feels boring.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 32,300ft of climbing on mountain bike stage race — gravel, technical does to your power file on race day.
162 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 162 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 162 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at La Ruta de los Conquistadores. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at La Ruta de los Conquistadores demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride mountain bike stage race — gravel, technical singletrack, jungle, volcanic ground, mud/river crossings, with some paved connectors at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 162 miles of mountain bike stage race — gravel, technical singletrack, jungle, volcanic ground, mud/river crossings, with some paved connectors in Jaco to Turrialba area, Costa Rica (2026 total distance/elevation not published — figures below are historical, vary by edition).
